candidates.applicability: Applies only to the fixed public split with the same features, label definition, and evaluation protocol used for the GaussianNB baseline. This is a system-integration comparison, not a claim of medical or scientific validity.
falsification: The linear-control explanation is falsified if logistic_regression does not exceed GaussianNB on the paired fixed-split comparison.
The nonlinear-tree-specific explanation is falsified if logistic_regression exceeds GaussianNB and matches or exceeds random_forest on the same paired examples.

Any classifier-family mechanism claim is falsified if logistic_regression and random_forest paired differences from GaussianNB are indistinguishable from zero or inconsistent in direction under the fixed protocol.
candidates.mechanism: Logistic regression serves as a regularized linear discriminative control. It tests whether an additive log-odds boundary can replicate any gain over GaussianNB. A positive logistic-regression gain without a random-forest-specific advantage would support a simple linear/discriminative or Gaussian-assumption-misspecification explanation. Failure to replicate while random_forest remains ahead would support the proposed nonlinear-interaction/tree-ensemble mechanism. If neither control shows a reliable positive difference, the result is more consistent with evaluation variance, class imbalance, or preprocessing artifacts.
predictions: If the small random_forest-over-GaussianNB advantage is due to a simple additive/linear discriminative boundary rather than nonlinear tree interactions, logistic_regression will also exceed GaussianNB on the fixed split, with a positive paired accuracy difference on the same test examples.

If the random_forest advantage specifically depends on nonlinear interactions or tree-ensemble variance reduction beyond a linear boundary, logistic_regression will not match or exceed random_forest on the fixed split; the paired difference (random_forest minus logistic_regression) will be positive.

If the apparent advantage is mainly an evaluation, preprocessing, or class-imbalance artifact affecting classifiers similarly, logistic_regression will not show a reliable positive paired difference over GaussianNB, and any observed differences will be small and inconsistent with a classifier-family mechanism.

If GaussianNB is already near the fixed-split ceiling, both logistic_regression and random_forest will show paired differences close to zero, failing to support either a linear or nonlinear classifier-family mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Only add_control is allowed. The observed random_forest vs GaussianNB effect is small and below the descriptive 0.02 threshold, so it does not establish a nonlinear ensemble mechanism. I choose the untested logistic_regression C=1.0 candidate as a linear discriminative control: if a simple additive boundary replicates the gain, the random_forest-specific nonlinear-interaction explanation is weakened; if logistic regression does not replicate it while random_forest remains ahead, the nonlinear/tree-ensemble mechanism gains specific support. The candidate's frozen config, metric, threshold, data, and seeds remain unchanged.
